sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: It was the night of March 30th, 2005,
sentences.zh: 那是2005年3月30日的夜晚，

sentences.en: and the Powerball jackpot was $25 million.
sentences.zh: 强力球彩票头奖高达2500万美元。

sentences.en: On TV, the white ping-pong balls rolled out one by one
sentences.zh: 电视上，白色的乒乓球一个接一个地滚出来，

sentences.en: as the host announced the winning numbers.
sentences.zh: 主持人宣布着中奖号码。

sentences.en: 22, 28, 32, 33, 39, and your Powerball is 42.
That's producer Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人埃弗里·特鲁夫曼。

sentences.en: And there was a winner in Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州出了一位中奖者。

sentences.en: But the way that Powerball drawings work,
sentences.zh: 但按照强力球开奖的规律，

sentences.en: there are usually some second-place winners
sentences.zh: 通常都会有一些二等奖得主，

sentences.en: who guess all of the numbers except for the very last one.
sentences.zh: 他们猜中了除了最后一个号码之外的所有数字。

sentences.en: On average, there are three or four of these players.
sentences.zh: 平均下来，这样的玩家有三到四个。

sentences.en: But on March 30th, 2005, there were 110 second-place winners.
sentences.zh: 但在2005年3月30日那天，有110位二等奖得主。

sentences.en: Was there a computer glitch that played all the same number?
sentences.zh: 是电脑故障摇出了全一样的号码吗？

sentences.en: Like, has someone compromised the system?
sentences.zh: 比如说，系统被人入侵了吗？

sentences.en: This is journalist Jennifer Aitley.
sentences.zh: 这是记者詹妮弗·艾特利。

sentences.en: Lottery officials are panicking, you know,
sentences.zh: 彩票官员们慌了神，你知道的，

sentences.en: because, like, something is up.
sentences.zh: 因为，呃，出大事了。

sentences.en: So the next day, as the winners around the United States came to collect,
sentences.zh: 于是第二天，当全美各地的中奖者前来领奖时，

sentences.en: the Powerball officials asked them,
sentences.zh: 强力球官员问他们：

sentences.en: So where'd you get your number from?
sentences.zh: 那你们的号码是从哪儿来的？

sentences.en: And each of them had the same answer.
sentences.zh: 每个人的回答都一样。

sentences.en: They had gotten their numbers from a fortune cookie.
sentences.zh: 他们的号码都是从幸运饼干里开出来的。

sentences.en: They were different cookies in different states,
sentences.zh: 在不同的州，饼干也不一样，

sentences.en: but they all had the same fortune and the same lucky numbers.
sentences.zh: 但它们都有着相同的签文和相同的幸运数字。

sentences.en: Very lucky numbers.
sentences.zh: 非常幸运的数字。

sentences.en: And so it just sort of made you realize, like,
sentences.zh: 所以这真让人意识到，

sentences.en: how much fortune cookies and Chinese food
sentences.zh: 幸运饼干和中餐

sentences.en: have become an American ritual.
sentences.zh: 在多大程度上已经成为了一种美国传统。

sentences.en: Chinese food, along with pizza and the Frankfurter,
sentences.zh: 中餐，连同披萨和法兰克福香肠一起，

sentences.en: has been adopted and modified to become American cuisine,
sentences.zh: 已经被本土化并改良成了美国菜，

sentences.en: rooted in some good old-fashioned American xenophobia.
sentences.zh: 其根源夹杂着一些老派的美国排外情绪。

sentences.en: In the early waves of Chinese immigration in the 1850s,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪50年代的早期华人移民潮中，

sentences.en: the new Chinese population worked mostly as miners and farmers and laborers.
sentences.zh: 新来的华人主要从事矿工、农民和劳工。

sentences.en: And Americans, as ever,
sentences.zh: 而美国人呢，一如既往地

sentences.en: were concerned about these new immigrants taking away jobs.
sentences.zh: 担心这些新移民会抢走工作。

sentences.en: And it was actually only after a huge anti-Chinese backlash
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是在一次大规模的排华逆流之后，

sentences.en: that the Chinese actually moved into two fields.
sentences.zh: 华人才真正转向了两个行业。

sentences.en: One was laundries, the other one was restaurants.
sentences.zh: 一个是洗衣店，另一个是餐馆。

sentences.en: So these were cleaning and cooking, which are women's work.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都是清洁和烹饪，属于妇女的工作。

sentences.en: And thus, they were safe and no longer a threat to the American male.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们是安全的，不再对美国男性构成威胁。

sentences.en: And as their livelihoods depended on it,
sentences.zh: 由于生计全系于此，

sentences.en: Chinese restaurant owners made up dishes to cater to American tastes.
sentences.zh: 中餐馆老板们发明了一些菜肴来迎合美国人的口味。

sentences.en: Americans basically like things that are sweet and they're fried and are chicken.
sentences.zh: 美国人基本上喜欢又甜、又炸、还是鸡肉的东西。

sentences.en: And that's how dishes like chop suey were invented.
sentences.zh: 杂碎这样的菜就是这样发明的。

sentences.en: Chop suey, the name, actually means assorted pieces, like odds and ends.
sentences.zh: 杂碎这个名字，实际上指的是各种碎料，就像零头碎脑的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, chop suey is the biggest culinary joke that one culture has ever played on another.
sentences.zh: 哦，杂碎是一个文化对另一个文化开过的最大饮食玩笑。

sentences.en: Chop suey is not a real Chinese dish at all.
sentences.zh: 杂碎根本不是一道真正的中国菜。

sentences.en: It's as American as apple pie.
sentences.zh: 它就像苹果派一样美国。

sentences.en: And speaking of apple pie...
sentences.zh: 说到苹果派……

sentences.en: Americans want dessert because we are American and we like things which are sweet and fatty.
sentences.zh: 美国人想要甜点，因为我们是美国人，我们喜欢又甜又油腻的东西。

sentences.en: So you needed a dessert.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一份甜点。

sentences.en: And as Chinese desserts go, there aren't that many options that the American palate would go for.
sentences.zh: 而在中式甜点中，符合美国人胃口的选择并没有那么多。

sentences.en: The Chinese desserts, like there is the mooncake, which like tastes and looks like a hockey puck.
sentences.zh: 说到中式甜点，比如月饼，吃起来和看起来都像个冰球。

sentences.en: But like there's not a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 不过也没太多选择。

sentences.en: And so around the 1920s, the fortune cookie somehow enters the American Chinese restaurant culture.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪20年代左右，幸运饼干不知怎么就进入了美式中餐文化。

sentences.en: Where they came from originally is a bit of a mystery.
sentences.zh: 它们最初源自何处有点像个谜。

sentences.en: But we'll get to that.
sentences.zh: 但我们待会儿会讲到。

sentences.en: First, let's make this perfectly clear.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们要把这一点彻底搞清楚。

sentences.en: The cookies are not from China.
sentences.zh: 这些饼干不是来自中国。

sentences.en: I don't know why, but Chinese, they don't eat fortune cookies.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么，但中国人根本不吃幸运饼干。

sentences.en: Stephen Yang is founder of Yang's Fortunes Incorporated in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·杨是旧金山杨氏财富有限公司的创始人。

sentences.en: Chinese people in China don't eat fortune cookies, but Americans consume billions of them.
sentences.zh: 中国本土的中国人不吃幸运饼干，但美国人却消耗了数十亿个。

sentences.en: Which means great business for Stephen.
sentences.zh: 这意味着斯蒂芬有着巨大的商机。

sentences.en: Because he prints a lot of the paper fortunes that go inside fortune cookies.
sentences.zh: 因为他印了大量塞进幸运饼干里的纸质签文。

sentences.en: If you go anywhere, New York, Boston, Houston, anywhere, oh, you can see my fortune.
sentences.zh: 如果你去任何地方，纽约、波士顿、休斯敦，任何地方，哦，你都能看到我的签文。

sentences.en: Including all the fortunes for Panda Express.
sentences.zh: 包括熊猫快餐的所有签文。

sentences.en: That's definitely Stephen's biggest client.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是斯蒂芬最大的客户。

sentences.en: Stephen's tiny warehouse in San Francisco's Dogpatch District is filled with boxes.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬位于旧金山多帕奇区的小仓库里堆满了箱子。

sentences.en: All stuffed full of tiny strips of fortune paper.
sentences.zh: 里面全塞满了细长的幸运签纸。

sentences.en: Each box contains 300,000 paper fortunes.
sentences.zh: 每个箱子里装着30万张签文。

sentences.en: I've printed lots of them.
sentences.zh: 我印了许许多多这样的签文。

sentences.en: I've printed lots of them.
sentences.zh: 我印了许许多多这样的签文。

sentences.en: See?
sentences.zh: 看吧？

sentences.en: And Stephen prints all these boxes and boxes with only five other employees.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬和仅有的另外五名员工一起印制了所有这些箱子。

sentences.en: And Lisa, Stephen's daughter, writes all the fortunes.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬的女儿丽莎负责写所有的签文。

sentences.en: When I visited, she was away on maternity leave.
sentences.zh: 我去拜访时，她正在休产假。

sentences.en: But she has written most of the company's 5,000 unique fortunes.
sentences.zh: 但公司那5000条独特的签文大都是她写的。

sentences.en: This is amazing, because when you think about it, fortunes are deceptively difficult to write.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了，因为仔细想想，签文看似简单，实则很难写。

sentences.en: The messages have to be really, really generic, because they could be for anyone.
sentences.zh: 这些信息必须非常非常大众化，因为它们可能适用于任何人。

sentences.en: You can't write messages like, you will meet a tall, dark stranger.
sentences.zh: 你不能写诸如“你会遇到一个高大英俊的黑发陌生人”之类的话。

sentences.en: Because an eight-year-old could read that and be like,
sentences.zh: 因为一个八岁小孩读到可能会觉得：

sentences.en: I don't want that.
sentences.zh: 我才不要那样的。

sentences.en: Why would we?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么会想要呢？

sentences.en: And fortunes also have to be careful not to offend.
sentences.zh: 而且签文还得小心翼翼，不能冒犯别人。

sentences.en: Famously, there was once a fortune that said, lighten up.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是，曾经有一条签文写着：看开点吧。

sentences.en: And a lot of customers were like, is this cookie calling me fat?
sentences.zh: 结果很多顾客都在想：这饼干是在说我胖吗？

sentences.en: And of course, no bad predictions.
sentences.zh: 当然，绝对不能有不好的预言。

sentences.en: Americans like their fortunes sunny.
sentences.zh: 美国人喜欢积极乐观的签文。

sentences.en: So fortunes tend to be vague, or just generally uplifting, like, tomorrow will be better.
sentences.zh: 所以签文往往比较模糊，或者总体上充满正能量，比如“明天会更好”。

sentences.en: Or the fortunes are nabbed from quotation books, just whatever Lisa can find.
sentences.zh: 或者干脆从名言警句里摘抄，只要是丽莎能找到的就行。

sentences.en: Stephen doesn't really care.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬其实并不在乎。

sentences.en: He doesn't read them.
sentences.zh: 他都不读这些签文。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: I make people, they like it.
sentences.zh: 我让大家开心，他们喜欢。

sentences.en: They say when they got a fortune, after eating dinner, they were keeping the words.
sentences.zh: 他们说拿到签文后，吃完晚饭，他们会把上面的话留着。

sentences.en: They keep them.
sentences.zh: 他们把签文留作纪念。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，千真万确。

sentences.en: Some people do keep the fortunes in their wallets.
sentences.zh: 有些人确实把签文放在钱包里。

sentences.en: When I asked around, it turns out a few of my friends do this,
sentences.zh: 当我四处打听时，发现我的几个朋友还真这么做过，

sentences.en: or can recite their favorite fortunes from memory.
sentences.zh: 或者能凭记忆背出他们最喜欢的签文。

sentences.en: And it's crazy, because a lot of these fortunes are Stevens, written by his daughter, Lisa.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了，因为这些签文很多都是斯蒂芬的，由他的女儿丽莎所写。

sentences.en: But there are a few ways to tell where your fortunes come from.
sentences.zh: 不过，还是有几种方法可以辨别你的签文来自哪里。

sentences.en: If you get one with blue corners on it, that was printed by a giant company in New York called Wonton Food.
sentences.zh: 如果你拿到一张边缘带蓝色的签文，那是纽约一家名为“幸运面食”的大公司印刷的。

sentences.en: They make over 4 million cookies a day, and were responsible for the cookie that made all those Powerball winners in 2005.
sentences.zh: 他们每天生产超过400万个饼干，2005年造就了所有那些强力球中奖者的饼干就是他们生产的。

sentences.en: If your fortune has smiley faces on it, it was probably printed by a Chinese company.
sentences.zh: 如果你的签文上有笑脸，那它很可能是由一家中国公司印刷的。

sentences.en: For the American market, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是针对美国市场的。

sentences.en: And if the fortune doesn't have blue corners or smiley faces, chances are it was one of the many thousands that Stevens prints in all different colors and fonts,
sentences.zh: 如果签文没有蓝色边缘也没有笑脸，那它很有可能是斯蒂芬印制的成千上万种采用各种颜色和字体的签文之一，

sentences.en: and sends to factories all over the country, including the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Company in a tiny alleyway in San Francisco's Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 并被运往全国各地的工厂，包括位于旧金山唐人街一条小巷里的金门幸运饼干公司。

sentences.en: The Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Company is pretty touristy.
sentences.zh: 金门幸运饼干公司充满了游客观光的商业气息。

sentences.en: It charges visitors 50 cents a photo, and doesn't actually have a very big cookie output.
sentences.zh: 它向游客收取每张照片50美分的费用，其实饼干的产量并不是很大。

sentences.en: Actually, calling this place a factory is kind of an overstatement.
sentences.zh: 事实上，把这个地方叫做工厂未免有点夸大其词了。

sentences.en: It's just one narrow room, with most of the space taken up by three hulking fortune cookie machines.
sentences.zh: 它只有一个狭窄的房间，大部分空间都被三台庞大的幸运饼干机器占据了。

sentences.en: Versions of machines that were invented by Edward Louie.
sentences.zh: 这些是爱德华·路易发明的机器的各种版本。

sentences.en: My father used to call his machine, like, his fourth child.
sentences.zh: 我父亲以前把他的机器当成是，嗯，他的第四个孩子。

sentences.en: He had three sons, and then the fourth was his baby.
sentences.zh: 他有三个儿子，然后第四个就是他的心肝宝贝。

sentences.en: Ming Louie, one of Edward's three sons, met me at the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Company.
sentences.zh: 明·路易，爱德华的三个儿子之一，在金门幸运饼干公司接待了我。

sentences.en: These fortune cookie machines are pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 这些幸运饼干机器非常简单。

sentences.en: They flatten round dabs of batter onto a conveyor belt,
sentences.zh: 它们把一团圆形的的面糊压扁在传送带上，

sentences.en: and a worker sits next to this belt and folds the hot cookies around the paper fortunes, one by one, by hand.
sentences.zh: 一个工人坐在传送带旁，把热饼干一个接一个地亲手包在纸质签文外面。

sentences.en: And we pick them off, as you see them doing here, fold it, and put them on a conveyor.
sentences.zh: 我们把它们拿起来，就像你在这里看到的一样，折叠好，然后放到传送带上。

sentences.en: Ming learned how to fold the cookies when he was around eight years old.
sentences.zh: 明在大约八岁时就学会了如何折叠饼干。

sentences.en: The Louie family used to have a fortune cookie company of their own.
sentences.zh: 路易家族以前拥有他们自己的幸运饼干公司。

sentences.en: And it was their whole life.
sentences.zh: 那是他们生活的全部。

sentences.en: Even during dinner, we took shifts.
sentences.zh: 甚至在吃晚饭时，我们都要轮流换班。

sentences.en: Somebody eats, the other one works.
sentences.zh: 一个人吃饭，另一个人干活。

sentences.en: That's how we did it, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样度过的，你知道的。

sentences.en: And we used to call ourselves the prisoners, and that was a famous saying.
sentences.zh: 我们以前把自己叫做囚犯，那曾是一句名言。

sentences.en: Help, I'm a prisoner in this fortune cookie factory, you know.
sentences.zh: “救命，我是这个幸运饼干厂里的囚犯”，你知道的。

sentences.en: Ming's father later developed the next generation of fortune cookie machines,
sentences.zh: 明的父亲后来开发了下一代幸运饼干机器，

sentences.en: a fully automated version, which also folds the cookie.
sentences.zh: 这是一种全自动版本，也能自动折叠饼干。

sentences.en: And because of this technology, fortune cookies are widely available and cheap enough that restaurants can give them out for free.
sentences.zh: 由于这项技术，幸运饼干变得随处可见，而且便宜到餐馆可以免费赠送。

sentences.en: No one in the Louie family really questioned where the cookies originated.
sentences.zh: 路易家族没有人真正去追问过饼干到底源自何方。

sentences.en: But it was a mystery that other people tried to solve.
sentences.zh: 但这是其他人试图解开的一个谜团。

sentences.en: People like Sally Osaki.
sentences.zh: 像莎莉·尾崎这样的人。

sentences.en: She knew they were not invented in China.
sentences.zh: 她知道这些不是在中国发明的。

sentences.en: What do you mean the Chinese fortune cookie?
sentences.zh: 你什么意思，中国幸运饼干？

sentences.en: It's Japanese.
sentences.zh: 它是日本的。

sentences.en: Sally Osaki is California born and raised, but her parents came from Japan in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 莎莉·尾崎在加州出生长大，但她的父母在20世纪初从日本来到美国。

sentences.en: When I was a child, the fortunes used to be in Japanese rather than the Chinese character.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，签文上面印的都是日语，而不是汉字。

sentences.en: And the cookies weren't something you'd get at the end of a meal at a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 而且这种饼干可不是你在餐馆吃完饭后能拿到的那种东西。

sentences.en: They'd come in a bag, you know, and mostly I know who we got them when I was a child was we would go see Japanese movies.
sentences.zh: 它们是用袋子装的，你知道的，我所知道我们小时候怎么得到它们的，大部分是我们去看日本电影的时候。

sentences.en: So in Sally's California childhood, the cookies were a casual snack.
sentences.zh: 所以在莎莉的加州童年时代，这种饼干只是一种休闲零食。

sentences.en: But if you trace them all the way back to their origins in Japan, you actually find them at a shrine.
sentences.zh: 但如果你一直追溯到它们在日本的起源，你会发现它们其实出自神社。

sentences.en: In Kyoto, and if you kind of walk around there, you will be able to find these Japanese bakers, like grilling fortune cookies.
sentences.zh: 在京都，如果你在那里四处走走，你会发现这些日本面包师在烤制幸运饼干。

sentences.en: Jennifer flew to the Hushimi Inaritai Sha shrine in Kyoto specifically to try them.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗特意飞到京都的伏见稻荷大社去尝尝它们。

sentences.en: But they're not like the fortune cookies we see in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但它们跟我们在美国看到的幸运饼干不一样。

sentences.en: They're like bigger and browner, and they're actually kind of have this like nutty, savory flavor.
sentences.zh: 它们个头更大、颜色更褐，而且实际上带有一种坚果般的咸香风味。

sentences.en: So they're more cracker-like.
sentences.zh: 所以它们更像是脆饼干。

sentences.en: But still, they're that same iconic fortune cookie shape we all know.
sentences.zh: 但它们仍然是我们所熟知的那个标志性的幸运饼干形状。

sentences.en: There's actually an old Japanese image of a baker folding these crackers, and it dates back to 1878,
sentences.zh: 其实有一张日本面包师折叠这种脆饼的老照片，可以追溯到1878年，

sentences.en: decades before the first reports of American fortune cookies.
sentences.zh: 比关于美国幸运饼干的最早报道还要早几十年。

sentences.en: One of the bakers that I spoke to thought that the fortune cookies they designed to look like a bell,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的一位面包师认为，他们设计的幸运饼干看起来像一个铃铛，

sentences.en: in part because there are bells all along the paths up into the shrines.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是因为通往神殿的小路沿途到处都是铃铛。

sentences.en: But then why don't we eat it after sushi?
sentences.zh: 但为什么我们不在吃完寿司后吃它呢？

sentences.en: Because like people were not eating sushi in like 1920.
sentences.zh: 因为在1920年代左右，人们根本不吃寿司。

sentences.en: When Japanese immigrants were opening businesses in the 1920s, there was no market for Japanese food.
sentences.zh: 当日本移民在20年代开店时，日本食品根本没有市场。

sentences.en: Again, like the Chinese immigrants before them, they pandered to American tastes.
sentences.zh: 同样，就像他们之前的中国移民一样，他们迎合了美国人的口味。

sentences.en: So a lot of the Japanese families ran a lot of Chinese restaurants.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多日本家庭经营了大量的中餐馆。

sentences.en: And these Japanese families ran American Chinese restaurants, full of chop suey and other faux Chinese cuisine.
sentences.zh: 这些日本家庭经营着美式中餐馆，里面充满了杂碎和其他仿制中餐。

sentences.en: And these Japanese owners would throw in a fortune cookie for dessert.
sentences.zh: 而且这些日本店主还会顺便送一个幸运饼干作为甜点。

sentences.en: When Sally was a kid, fortune cookies were still made in Japanese bakeries in both L.A.
sentences.zh: 莎莉小时候，洛杉矶

sentences.en: and San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 和旧金山的日本面包店里还在制作幸运饼干。

sentences.en: And the fortunes were still in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 而且里面的签语还是日文的。

sentences.en: And then something happened that completely disrupted everything about Japanese American life in this country.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件事，彻底打乱了这个国家日裔美国人生活的方方面面。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know if you know that the Japanese Americans, 120,000 of us, during World War II were sent away to concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我不知道你是否知道，二战期间，我们有12万日裔美国人被送往集中营。

sentences.en: I was nine years old when we got sent to the concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 我们被送往集中营时我九岁。

sentences.en: Sally and her family were farmers in Fresno.
sentences.zh: 莎莉和她的家人是弗雷斯诺的农民。

sentences.en: They were summoned to a train station and sent off to a camp in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 他们被召集到火车站，并被送往亚利桑那州的一个集中营。

sentences.en: You had to carry whatever you were taking.
sentences.zh: 你只能带上手头随身携带的东西。

sentences.en: I was a child.
sentences.zh: 我当时还是个孩子。

sentences.en: I couldn't carry that much.
sentences.zh: 我拿不了那么多东西。

sentences.en: I carried a small suitcase.
sentences.zh: 我只带了一个小手提箱。

sentences.en: And I remember my mother took me to a store near our town to buy boots.
sentences.zh: 我记得母亲带我去我们镇附近的一家商店买靴子。

sentences.en: Because she heard that where we were going in Arizona, desert in Arizona, there were rattlesnakes and scorpions.
sentences.zh: 因为她听说我们要去的亚利桑那州，亚利桑那州的沙漠里有响尾蛇和蝎子。

sentences.en: Were there?
sentences.zh: 真的有吗？

sentences.en: Oh, there were, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，真的有，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Gila monsters and scorpions and rattlesnakes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 希拉毒蜥、蝎子和响尾蛇，是的。

sentences.en: In the camp, her parents were given jobs that earned hardly any money.
sentences.zh: 在营地里，她的父母被分配了几乎赚不到什么钱的工作。

sentences.en: Top salary was like $16 or $18 a month, a month.
sentences.zh: 最高薪水大约是一个月16或18美元，一个月。

sentences.en: For four years, from 1942 to 1946, California's Japanese and Japanese American community was marooned in the desert.
sentences.zh: 在1942年到1946年的四年里，加州的日本和日裔美国人社区被困在了沙漠中。

sentences.en: Out of sight, out of communication, and out of business.
sentences.zh: 远离视线，与世隔绝，无法营业。

sentences.en: Including a lot of Japanese bakers and Japanese restaurant owners.
sentences.zh: 其中包括许多日本面包师和日本餐馆老板。

sentences.en: My recollection was that after we came out of the camps, it was the Chinese fortune cookie.
sentences.zh: 我的记忆是，在我们离开集中营后，出现的就成了中国幸运饼干。

sentences.en: The Chinese actually commercialized it and all the Chinese restaurants started to serve it.
sentences.zh: 中国人实际上将其商业化了，所有中餐馆都开始提供它。

sentences.en: Thanks to Chinese business owners, and later, Edward Louie's fortune cookie machines,
sentences.zh: 多亏了中国企业主，以及后来爱德华·刘易斯的幸运饼干机器，

sentences.en: the Chinese American fortune cookie, as we now know it, flourished.
sentences.zh: 正如我们现在所知的美籍华人幸运饼干繁荣发展起来。

sentences.en: It's nearly impossible to pin the Americanization of the cookie to one specific Japanese American baker or Chinese American restaurant.
sentences.zh: 几乎不可能将饼干的美国化归功于某一个特定的日裔美国面包师或美籍华人餐馆。

sentences.en: The transfer from Japanese cracker to American Chinese cookie was a larger phenomenon that occurred, more or less, across California.
sentences.zh: 从日本脆饼到美式中餐饼干的转变是一个更大的现象，或多或少发生在整个加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: And then swept the rest of the United States.
sentences.zh: 然后席卷了美国其余地区。

sentences.en: And then the world.
sentences.zh: 然后是全世界。

sentences.en: Except for China.
sentences.zh: 中国除外。

sentences.en: They still don't eat fortune cookies.
sentences.zh: 他们至今仍不吃幸运饼干。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Avery Truffelman with Katie Mingles, Sam Greenspan, Kurt Kolstead, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%无形》由艾弗里·特雷弗曼与凯蒂·明格斯、萨姆·格林斯潘、库尔特·科尔斯特德以及我罗马·马尔斯共同制作。

sentences.en: This episode was largely inspired by Jennifer A.
sentences.zh: 这一集很大程度上受到了詹妮弗·A·

sentences.en: Lee's book, The Fortune Cookie Chronicles,
sentences.zh: 李的书《幸运饼干编年史》的启发，

sentences.en: which goes into even more depth about the origins of American Chinese cuisine.
sentences.zh: 该书更深入地探讨了美式中餐的起源。

sentences.en: And believe me, there are way deeper depths.
sentences.zh: 相信我，还有更深的水深。

sentences.en: It's a great read.
sentences.zh: 这是一本非常值得一读的书。

sentences.en: But these days, Jennifer's got a new passion project that needs your help.
sentences.zh: 但如今，詹妮弗有一个需要你帮助的新热情项目。

sentences.en: Designers?
sentences.zh: 设计师们？

sentences.en: We have this great project with the White House and the Europe Public Library,
sentences.zh: 我们与白宫和欧洲公共图书馆有一个伟大的项目，

sentences.en: where we're inviting everyone to redesign covers for public domain books.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请每个人为公共领域书籍重新设计封面。

sentences.en: They still need covers for titles like Peter Pan and The Secret Garden.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然需要像《彼得潘》和《秘密花园》这样作品的封面。

sentences.en: You can learn more about it at recoveringtheclassics.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以在recoveringtheclassics.com了解更多信息。

sentences.en: Special thanks to John Schmidt and Mitsuko Crape.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢约翰·施密特和三津子·克雷普。

sentences.en: Lulatone provided all the lovely music for the show this week.
sentences.zh: Lulatone为本期节目提供了所有动听的音乐。

sentences.en: And if you're interested in learning more about America's Japanese concentration camps,
sentences.zh: 如果你有兴趣了解更多关于美国日裔集中营的信息，

sentences.en: Sally Osaki highly recommends the book Infamy by Richard Reeves.
sentences.zh: 莎莉·尾崎极力推荐理查德·里夫斯的书《耻辱》。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is a project of 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced out of the offices of ArcSign,
sentences.zh: 《99%无形》是旧金山91.7 KALW的项目，由ArcSign办公室制作，

sentences.en: an architecture and interiors firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: ArcSign是一家位于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心的建筑和室内设计公司。

sentences.en: Right next to Oakland's Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 就在奥克兰唐人街旁边。

sentences.en: And if you're ever in Oakland's Chinatown, you gotta go to Angel Feet on 9th.
sentences.zh: 如果你有机会去奥克兰的唐人街，你一定要去9街的天使之足。

sentences.en: Get your feet rubbed.
sentences.zh: 去按按摩脚吧。

sentences.en: It'll make your life better.
sentences.zh: 这会让你的生活变得更好。

sentences.en: It's an unpaid endorsement for getting your feet rubbed.
sentences.zh: 这是一次关于去足疗的无偿推荐。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并点赞这个节目。

sentences.en: We're all on Twitter, Tumblr, Instagram, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们都在Twitter、Tumblr、Instagram和Spotify上。

sentences.en: But you can listen to every single episode of 99% Invisible and see pictures at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但你可以在99pi.org上收听《99%无形》的每一期节目并查看图片。
